title: ChatGPT suggests tethered cord syndrome for a child seen by 17 doctors over three years; pediatric neurosurgeon confirms and operates
summary: Mother entered son's MRI notes and symptoms into ChatGPT; it suggested tethered cord syndrome, confirmed and operated on by a neurosurgeon.
account: In 2023 Courtney, mother of Alex, entered his magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) notes and symptom observations line by line into ChatGPT. Alex's chronic pain began at age 4 during the COVID-19 lockdown. He went on to grind his teeth, stop growing taller and drag his left foot. 17 physicians over three years had found no diagnosis. ChatGPT suggested tethered cord syndrome. She booked a new neurosurgeon, Dr Holly Gilmer of the Michigan Head & Spine Institute. Gilmer reviewed the MRI, found spina bifida occulta with a tethered cord and operated to release it. That was a few weeks before the TODAY.com report (11 September 2023, updated 12 September 2023). Alex was still recovering. The month of the ChatGPT query and the surgery date are not given.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational assistant built to answer user prompts. Producing a diagnostic hypothesis from entered clinical notes is an instance of that general function, not a designed or validated medical capability.
segment: Caregiver-initiated use of a consumer LLM

ratings.reason: A child with three years of chronic pain, mobility problems and growth delay received a diagnosis and corrective spinal surgery. The report describes him as recovering, so the benefit is life-changing but not shown to be life-saving.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT produced the hypothesis (tethered cord syndrome) that the mother took to a new neurosurgeon. The diagnosis itself was made by the neurosurgeon from the existing MRI, and the treatment was surgical. ChatGPT's contribution was ending the diagnostic search. The source is a news report quoting the mother and treating neurosurgeon, not a peer-reviewed case report.

fields.account: In 2023 Courtney, mother of Alex, entered his magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) notes and symptom observations line by line into ChatGPT. Alex's chronic pain began at age 4 during the COVID-19 lockdown. He went on to grind his teeth, stop growing taller and drag his left foot. 17 physicians over three years had found no diagnosis. ChatGPT suggested tethered cord syndrome. She booked a new neurosurgeon, Dr Holly Gilmer of the Michigan Head & Spine Institute. Gilmer reviewed the MRI, found spina bifida occulta with a tethered cord and operated to release it. That was a few weeks before the TODAY.com report (11 September 2023, updated 12 September 2023). Alex was still recovering. The month of the ChatGPT query and the surgery date are not given.
